# vuln-digest

> Instructions that an AI assistant follows to set up a scheduled digest of new vulnerabilities for its user: an interview about the user's stack, a profile, durable state, a schedule, delivery, and the steps of every run - fetch, deduplicate, match to the stack, rate, say what to do.

The instructions are one document. An assistant reads it when the user asks for a vulnerability digest, asks the user a few questions, sets up the scheduled job, and shows a test digest. A small helper script does the fetching and the deduplication.

## Docs

- [vuln-digest instructions](https://vuln-digest.secmy.app/README.md): the full document as plain Markdown - the working rules, 7 setup steps (0-6), the run steps, the digest format and the sources
- [Full text in one file](https://vuln-digest.secmy.app/llms-full.txt): the same document, for tools that look for llms-full.txt
- [Current version](https://vuln-digest.secmy.app/version.json): JSON with the current version of the instructions and a summary of each release, for jobs that run from a saved copy
- [Helper script](https://vuln-digest.secmy.app/vuln_feed.py): Python, standard library only - fetches Zero Wire, CISA KEV, OSV, vendor RSS or Atom feeds, GitHub Security Advisories and NVD by CPE, adds EPSS and CVE.org details, checks feeds, and remembers what was delivered

## Contributing

- [AGENTS.md](https://vuln-digest.secmy.app/AGENTS.md): how to build, check and change vuln-digest itself, for agents that edit its repository

## Optional

- [Instructions as a web page](https://vuln-digest.secmy.app/docs/): the same document rendered for people, with a table of contents
- [Landing page](https://vuln-digest.secmy.app/): a short overview for people, with the prompt to paste into an assistant
- [Source repository](https://github.com/SecH0us3/vuln-digest): history, issues and pull requests
